messages:

Subject: Kickoff: model & token sizing for triage assistant

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the quick call earlier. Per our discussion, Atlas is building a clinical triage assistant that will ingest patient intake notes (avg ~700 tokens) plus prior visit context when available (up to ~4k tokens), and return structured triage recommendations plus brief rationales. A few specifics:

- Expected active users: 3,000 clinicians (web UI) with a 10% daily active rate for the initial pilot.
- Average session: 2–3 queries per clinician.
- Latency target: <350ms 95th for short queries, <700ms for long-context queries (if possible).
- Security: must be deployed in Redwood Private (VPC); we will provide SOC2 evidence during procurement.

Can you send a recommended model shortlist (with context-length recommendations), a ballpark monthly token projection, and any immediate integration blockers we should be aware of? We want a short write-up to share with our engineering lead by Monday.

Thanks,
Tom Rivera
Director, Clinical AI
Atlas Health

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model & token sizing for triage assistant

Tom — great to meet earlier, and appreciate the specifics. Below is a concise model shortlist and a first-pass monthly token projection based on the numbers you shared. Ben & Monica are looped for technical sizing and Private deployment notes.

Shortlist (recommendation order):
1) redwood-clarity-8k (recommended) — native 8k context, strong safety priors for medical text, best cost/perf for structured output.
2) redwood-clarity-32k (fallback for full-visit context) — use for batched long-context jobs or async review flows.
3) open-instruct-13b-quant (cost-optimized) — good for short queries; consider for high-volume non-sensitive paths.

Context guidance and routing:
- Default route: redwood-clarity-8k for UI queries. If payload exceeds ~7.5k tokens, automatically route to redwood-clarity-32k and surface progress to the user (async).
- For privacy, all production traffic should go through your Private deployment with KMS-managed keys.

Monthly token projection (pilot):
- Active clinicians/day: 300 (10% of 3,000)
- Queries/day: 300 * 2.5 avg = 750
- Avg tokens/query (input + output): 900 (700 intake + 200 response)
- Daily tokens: 750 * 900 = 675,000
- Monthly (30d): ~20.25M tokens

Notes: routing a fraction (~10–15%) of sessions to the 32k model for long-context recall bumps the monthly token usage by ~2–3M tokens. If you enable prefix caching for prior visit context, expect a 25–40% effective token reduction on repeat visits.

Attachments: I’m attaching a short model_shortlist_notes.csv and an initial throughput calc from Ben. Monica — can you confirm any infra constraints for Private (VPC peering window, expected turnaround) and whether the atlas_context_profile.xlsx has everything you need for onboarding?

Next steps:
- Ben to share throughput/instance sizing + expected latency.
- Monica to confirm Private onboarding window & SOC2 evidence checklist.
- Tom to confirm whether async long-context flows are acceptable for the 32k model.

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up Monday.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: model & token sizing for triage assistant — throughput & instance calc

Tom / Hannah — quick technical note and attached throughput calc (pdf). Summary of findings for the pilot traffic profile Hannah shared:

- Baseline: redwood-clarity-8k on a single A100-style instance (dedicated) gives ~110 concurrent short-query QPS with avg token-generation latency ~120ms for 200-token outputs.
- For your pilot (750 QPS-equivalent daily across the day -> concurrency peaks ~45), two instances in a dedicated pool with autoscale to 4 during peak should comfortably hit the latency SLO.
- Memory: 8k-context model requires ~32GB GPU memory footprint per replica when using our quantized path. 32k variant is ~48–56GB depending on kernel selection.
- Cost estimate (hosted-equivalent for reference): ~2.4M tokens/month on 8k route ≈ cost tier X; I’ll leave exact $ to commercial.

Practical suggestions:
- Enable prefix caching for prior visit context; this reduces avg token generation by up to 35% for repeat patients and lowers effective GPU time.
- If you need sub-400ms 95th on long-context queries, consider batching with async responses or pre-compute embeddings+retrieval for history to reduce autoregressive decoding.

I’ve attached redwood_throughput_calc.pdf with the assumptions and the concurrency math. Happy to review with your infra team.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

1) SOC2 & evidence: please upload the cert + any customer-facing attestation to the linked Drive folder. We will include the SOC2 pointer in the procurement packet. (See related link above.)
2) VPC peering / network: estimated window to complete peering and routing rules — 5 business days after we receive your network CIDRs and peering approval. If you need a faster window, we can provision a temporary VPN tunnel for the pilot.
3) Keys & logging: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integration. For audit logs, we will provide token-level request tracing (retention per contract).
4) Onboarding timeline (pilot):
   - Week 0: network & key exchange + simple smoke tests (3–5 days)
   - Week 1: deploy redwood-clarity-8k, configure prefix caching, run load test
   - Week 2: tune routing rules and run a 48-hour pilot with select clinicians

Deliverables I need from Atlas to move forward: network CIDR, list of pilot clinician accounts (sample), and confirmation on async long-context flows (yes/no).

I’ll open a ticket with our onboarding ops and assign an onboarding engineer once we have the CIDR. If you want, I can also include a short checklist for your security team to expedite the SOC2 evidence request.

Tom — let me know if Monday's sync at 10am PT still works and I’ll send a calendar invite.
